author: reek
body: Every boot-keyboard interface on the bus is bound, not only the first. codex-vm's default topology carries TWO keyboards -- one on root port 2 and one behind the high-speed hub on root port 4 -- and until this test nothing asserted that the second is reachable while the first is alive.

author: reek
body: `-hid-keys` routes the scripted keys through the USB HID model alone: no PS/2 queue, no host-side write into the key cell. `got=30` therefore proves a scancode travelled interrupt-IN DMA, drain and decode end to end, which no bed test had ever shown -- injected keys used to reach the guest through the PS/2 emulation whatever the USB stack did.

author: reek
body: The injected keys appear on the ROOT keyboard here, so the primary's sticky non-zero count must move and the hub peer's must stay zero: the peer delivers the all-zero idle reports of a keyboard nobody types on.

author: reek
body: The wait is bounded by the RTC rather than by an iteration count: each pump costs several VM exits, so a count large enough to cover the key timeline in iterations is minutes of wall clock.
